correctness.rationale: Independent exhaustive replay visits all 131,070 strings at lengths 1–16, tests primitivity and every cyclic conjugate using exact binary prefix/suffix counts, and finds no qualifiers through 15 and 96 at 16. Each qualifying word has eight ones; the six least rotations and the full shortest-border vectors match RESULT.md. The six canonical-root lengths in the stated order are 8,8,8,6,8,4. Primitivity gives orbit size 16; explicit dihedral/complement comparison gives three pairs of necklaces. The two bundled implementations corroborate the count, but do not explicitly check the reversal/complement classification. The independent replay does. Taking complements of the compared factors inside the whole word proves that border lengths k and n-k are equivalent; in particular the frozen half-length cutoff is exhaustive. Nothing about larger lengths follows from this run.

value.rationale: The natural question is where the primitive-word obstruction for ordinary borders first fails when equality is replaced by Abelian equivalence. A prior witness alone does not identify that boundary. A complete list of the first counterexamples supplies all minimal tests for structural conjectures about the circular property, not merely further examples or an arbitrary finite count.
